9856.t: Etymology tree the BMAC substratebor.? Proto-Indo-Iranian *síndʰuš ▲ Proto-Indo-Iranian *síndʰuš Sanskrit सिन्धु॑ (síndhu)bor. Old Persian 𐏃𐎡𐎯𐎢𐏁 (hiⁿdūš)bor.

9878.t: From earlier *ὁπός (*hopós), which underwent Ionic psilosis, from Proto-Indo-European *sokʷos (“juice, resin”).

9820.t: No etymology. Furnée connects the word with ἰξύς (ixū́s, “loins”) assuming a common Pre-Greek origin.

9850.t: A Pre-Greek word without further etymology.

9851.t: Perhaps a nominal formation from ἴλλω (íllō, “to press together”), from Proto-Indo-European *wi-wl-e, a reduplicative formation from Proto-Indo-European *wel- (“to press together”), whence also εἴλω (eílō, “to shut in, press”); see there for more discussion.

9863.t: Perhaps from the same root as ὀδύνη (odúnē, “pain”).

9808.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hihwákʰō, reduplicated form from Proto-Indo-European *sweh₂gʰ-.

9812.t: A hypostasis *ἐν-γνύ-α (*en-gnú-a, “place in the knee”). The stem ἰγνύς (ignús) was formed after ἰξύς (ixús, “waist, loins”) and ὀσφῦς (osphûs, “hips or loins”).

9809.t: Probably from Proto-Indo-European *h₁eysh₂-n-ye-ti, a nasal ye-present of *h₁eysh₂- (“to strengthen, propel”), whence also Sanskrit इषण्यति (iṣaṇyati, “to urge on, incite”) (though the semantics are not particularly strong, nor particularly weak).

9862.t: From ὀγδοήκοντα (ogdoḗkonta, “eighty”) + -στός (-stós), a variant of -τός (-tós, ordinal suffix).

9810.t: From ἰατρεύω (īātreúō, “to treat medically, to cure”) + -εῖον (-eîon).
